successors.name: Abe clan
successors.text: the Emishi domains of northern Honshu left after 802: Aomori, northern Iwate, most of Akita and Yamagata, under the Abe general who 'levied taxes and confiscated property on his own' in 1050

ledger.x: 478: the Chinese Book of Song records '55 kingdoms' of the hairy people in the East; the Emishi page's first dated mention.
709: the court founds the fort of Ideha near Akita.
724: Taga Fort rises on the Sendai plain.
794: bookkeeping handoff: the court moves to Heian-kyo and the war goes on (nara-japan dossier ends the contest here; the fighting runs to 811).
794: the war under the Heian court.
811: the Thirty-Eight Years' War is over.
1051: the Abe, 'the general overseeing the Emishi', break with the court.

wars.name: Abe no Hirafu's northern expeditions
wars.outcome: No land change recorded: the 180-ship expedition reached Aguta (Akita), allied with the Aguta, Tsugaru and Watarishima Emishi and, on the Akita Castle page, set up a fortification on the Mogami River.

wars.name: Thirty-Eight Years' War
wars.outcome: The Isawa Emishi under Aterui won at the Koromo River in 789 and surrendered in 802; the war was over in 811.

wars.name: Former Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: Imperial victory at Kuriyagawa in 1062; Abe no Sadato surrendered.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the page names forts and rivers (Taga, Momonofu, the Kitakami), never a boundary; the Kitakami line after 802 is the page's own words.
